claims.statement: The European Commission states that the EUDAMED UDI/Devices module became mandatory to use on 28 May 2026.
The Commission says manufacturers must submit UDI/device information for devices they place on the EU market, and EMDN is the nomenclature used for EUDAMED device registration.
Commission transition material gives 28 November 2026 as the deadline to register relevant devices in the UDI/Devices module during the transition.

contrary_evidence: EUDAMED is the official database and provides documentation and a helpdesk, so low-volume manufacturers can register directly.
Mandatory use has already begun, so some manufacturers will have completed migration before a new vendor reaches market.
Different device classes and legacy-device transition rules increase specialization and reduce the benefit of a broad generic product.

economics.acquisition_route: Contract a senior regulatory advisor, recruit two low-risk device makers through medtech incubators, and distribute the proven migration workflow through advisors
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 5-8 year scenario: 80 manufacturers averaging 75,000 PLN annual revenue yields 6.0m PLN; at 30% EBITDA, 4x, and 75% ownership, equity value is about 5.4m PLN.
economics.founder_time: 18-24 hours per week for a tightly bounded device segment; regulatory review and validation remain with named specialists
economics.gross_margin_basis: Schema validation, reconciliation, and exports are software-like; regulatory mapping and dirty legacy cleanup are expert services that must be scoped
economics.payback: Customer payback hypothesis: reducing portfolio migration errors and repeated data reconciliation can justify 40,000-120,000 PLN annually for nontrivial portfolios; compare with regulatory-operations labor
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 20,000-70,000 PLN migration and 30,000-100,000 PLN annual subscription based on active device and change volume
economics.retention_or_repeat: New devices, identifiers, certificates, labels, countries, and changes depend on the same master graph; QMS and EUDAMED reconciliation creates high switching cost

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A clean longitudinal graph of devices, identifiers, certificates, labels, and changes lowers each future submission cost and makes errors easier to detect
fingerprint.customer: Small EU medical-device and IVD manufacturers or authorised representatives with dozens to hundreds of devices and limited regulatory operations staff
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: EU MDR/IVDR consultants, authorised representatives, QMS implementers, incubators, and UDI issuing-agency service partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Data intake, field validation, EMDN/identifier workflow, label/EUDAMED reconciliation, approvals, and change evidence; hypothesis 20,000-70,000 PLN migration plus 30,000-100,000 PLN annually
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Regulatory affairs or quality leader pays portfolio migration/onboarding and an annual master-data license, with metered change submissions
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Mandatory EUDAMED rollout, first market placement, new Basic UDI-DI/device, label change, certificate change, or portfolio migration

founder_fit: Founder has health, biosignal, and data-science context relevant to medtech data structures
Girlfriend's medical training may help surface workflow questions but does not substitute for regulatory or clinical expertise
High-value, low-volume B2B product suits analytical work and limited public exposure
Can be validated with synthetic portfolios before any sensitive customer data is processed
risks: Medical-device errors can have patient-safety and market-access consequences
Regulatory consultants and enterprise product-information systems are strong incumbents
Small manufacturers may have too few devices to justify recurring software
Security, auditability, and vendor qualification can make sales cycles long

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulated product-master-data hub sold per manufacturer and active device family
structure.control_point: The approved UDI/device master record synchronized across QMS, label, issuing-agency identifier, and mandatory EUDAMED registration
structure.critical_dependency: Correct regulatory classification and identifier ownership, validated manufacturer data, and authorized EUDAMED actor/module access

thesis: Planning-stage hypothesis: create a controlled device-master-data workflow for small medical-device and IVD manufacturers or authorised representatives that maps QMS/product data into UDI identifiers, EMDN classifications, EUDAMED fields, labels, and change-controlled submissions. The service would not make clinical or conformity judgments; regulatory specialists approve those. The product's control point is the reconciled master record used before a device is placed on the market and whenever device data changes. Starting with a narrow segment such as medical-device software or low-risk Polish manufacturers can keep the schema and liability bounded while the mandatory EUDAMED rollout creates a timely migration event.
title: EUDAMED UDI Master-Data Operations
uncertainties: Best low-liability device niche and number of underserved manufacturers
Permitted technical mechanisms for submission or bulk upload under client authority
Extent of legacy-data cleanup required before software can add value
Whether authorised representatives will resell or build the workflow themselves
